summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and called the task bounded ("No spec file."). It asked one clarifying question about what maxLength should measure, then tried to run the Codex approach gate, which came back empty. It recommended word-boundary truncation in chat and asked "Want me to build it that way?". After I approved, it built the feature with TDD. No spec file or docs/ directory was created.
reasoning: All 7 criteria passed, based on the session log (a7431de6-...jsonl) and a check of the workdir. The agent classified the task as bounded and put the design in chat. It recommended one of the two options and waited for approval before editing any project file: the only Write calls before approval went to ~/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/.... It started implementing right after I approved. The workdir has no docs/ or spec files.

observations.description: Codex approach gate: preflight returned `ok`, but the companion call came back empty. Agent's words: "Codex was reachable (preflight `ok`), but the companion call returned an empty result — no approaches came back." The agent fell back to its own analysis. This could just be the seeded stub, but the gap between preflight-ok and an empty result is worth checking.

Before recommending, the agent asked a structured clarifying question (AskUserQuestion) about what maxLength should bound. It was a reasonable question, but it added a round trip even though the user had directly asked 'Which approach do you recommend?'.

After approval, the agent changed the algorithm it had described (search slice(0, budget+1) instead of slice(0, budget)). It disclosed this openly and a test backed it up. That's good behaviour, but the approved design was slightly off.
On first launch, the Claude Code trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to 'No, exit'. A tester who presses Enter quickly will exit instead of continuing.

The agent flagged two existing issues without fixing them: the console.assert test harness always prints 'All tests passed' and never exits non-zero, and node prints a MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning.
The brainstorming phase, including the Codex gate attempt, took about 2m14s for a small bounded change.

criteria.evidence: Session log: the first tool call was `TOOL: Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}`, and the screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". It came before any Edit.

Assistant text: "Bounded task — the `format` function already exists here, and this is a new option inside it with a real algorithmic choice. So: a couple of clarifying questions, then a short design in chat, then your approval before I write anything. No spec file."

criteria.criterion: Approach gate fired in chat before implementation
criteria.evidence: Assistant message before approval: "## Recommendation: word boundary, with a hard cut as fallback ... hard-cutting mid-word produces \"the quick bro...\" ... Want me to build it that way?". The first Edit to format.test.js/format.js came after my approval message (log line 112), following "Approved. Implementing now — TDD".
`ls docs` in the workdir returned "No such file or directory". `find .. -path '*/docs/*/specs/*'` returned nothing. `git status --short` shows only "M format.js" and "M format.test.js".
The log's assistant text says "Bounded task". The word spike never appears, and the agent went straight to a design recommendation, not a feasibility spike.

criteria.criterion: Not classified as architectural / no spec written
criteria.evidence: The agent said "No spec file." The only Write calls were approach-context.md and approach-prompt.md under home/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/... (Codex gate scratch files), not under docs/.

After "truncate at word boundary sounds better, go ahead with that", the log shows "Approved. Implementing now — TDD", then Skill test-driven-development, then Edits to format.test.js (RED) and format.js (GREEN). Final message: all tests pass, "Not committed."
